title: Multi-LLM Collaboration + Data-Centric Innovation = 2x Better Vulnerability Repair
structure_gain: Removing serialized AST sequence drops EM by 1.0pp (20.0%->19.0%); removing CWE knowledge drops it 1.1pp; removing full-function input drops it 1.2pp, all on the same adapted-CodeT5 backbone and training budget
stop_detail: No automated grounding/stop mechanism; qualitative case study only (Sec 6.1), relies on assumed perfect fault localization via special tokens marking vulnerable lines

title: Security Vulnerability Detection with Multitask Self-Instructed Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

key_numbers.metric: F1 on BigVul (vs best baseline LineVul+DeepDFA)
F1 on PreciseBugs (post-cutoff, unseen) vs LineVul
GNN-embedding ablation on BigVul (MSIVD- vs MSIVD)

structure_gain: Adding CFG/DFA-derived GGNN embeddings to the fine-tuned LLM's hidden states raises F1 from 0.90 (LLM-only, MSIVD-) to 0.92 (MSIVD) on BigVul, holding the CodeLlama-13B backbone and training budget fixed (Table 4).
stop_detail: Reaching-definition dataflow analysis computed over each function's CFG is embedded via a GGNN and concatenated to the LLM's final hidden states before classification (Section 3.3).

title: LProtector: An LLM-driven Vulnerability Detection System
structure_gain: Removing RAG context (holding GPT-4o and CoT fixed) drops F1 from 33.49% to 23.92%, a 9.57pp loss (Table III).
stop_detail: Input code is embedded via OpenAI embeddings; top-5 cosine-similar CWE/CVE examples are retrieved from a 500-instance Big-Vul vector store (ChromaDB); GPT-4o selects the best-matching exemplar to ground its classification (RAG formula, Sec III).

title: Context-Enhanced Vulnerability Detection Based on Large Language Model

key_numbers.metric: F1, DeepSeek-R1+CoT: API-abstraction level A3 vs w/o-API context
F1 vs best context-sampling baseline (API-guided sampling)
CodeLLaMA+BP F1 vs best baseline (hierarchy sampling, HS-C)

structure_gain: A3 API-context vs w/o-API: F1 69.09% vs 60.89% (+8.20pp), same model (Table 4).
stop_detail: Control-flow and data-flow analysis over the target function and its callees (up to 3 call layers) extracts four API-usage features (fuzzy/concrete branches, call counts, key variables) at four increasing abstraction levels A1-A4, appended directly into the LLM prompt (Section 3.2.2, 3.3.1).

title: CognixShield: PoV-Guided Vulnerable API Usage Detection in Large Codebases via LLMs

key_numbers.value: 89% full; 64% w/o AST fragmentation; 60% w/o cross-file RAG; 77% w/o PoV guidance

structure_gain: w/o cross-file RAG (single-function context only) drops F1 from 89% to 60% (-29pp); w/o AST-based fragmentation drops F1 to 64% (-25pp); w/o PoV-guided reasoning drops F1 to 77% (-12pp), all on the same 57-project dataset
stop_detail: Reflector agent's retrieval loop terminates when it judges the assembled context provides sufficient inter-procedural coverage for exploitability determination or no new relevant fragments are retrieved (multi-agent RAG loop, Reflector/Grader description)

title: SecureFixAgent: A Hybrid LLM Agent for Automated Python Static Vulnerability Repair

key_numbers.value: +13.51pp fix accuracy vs pre-trained LLMs; -10.8pp FP vs static analysis alone; -5.46pp FP vs pre-trained LLMs

structure_gain: No representation-only ablation; reported gain is from the iterative validate-loop vs single-pass LLM: fix accuracy rises from 79.72% (LLM-only, converges at iteration 1) to 87.83% (SecureFixAgent, converges at iteration 3) (Fig. 2, Table III).
stop_detail: Bandit static-analysis findings (vulnerable segment, rule report) plus full source are fed to the LLM each iteration, and each proposed patch is re-validated by re-running Bandit until convergence or the iteration limit (Algorithm 1, Sec III-B/III-E).

title: Retrieval-Augmented Few-Shot Prompting Versus Fine-Tuning for Code Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.value: Fine-tuned Gemini-1.5-Flash 59.31% F1 vs Fine-tuned CodeBERT 91.22% F1

structure_gain: Retrieval-augmented 20-shot prompting raises F1 from 36.35% (zero-shot) to 74.05%, same Gemini-1.5-Flash model (Table I) -- retrieval of semantically similar labeled examples is the sole varied factor across the few-shot arms.
stop_detail: Query code is embedded via gemini-embedding-001; top-k semantically similar labeled code+vulnerability-label pairs are retrieved via cosine similarity from a ChromaDB store and inserted as few-shot exemplars in the prompt (retrieval mechanism section).

title: Reducing False Positives in Static Bug Detection with LLMs: An Empirical Study in Industry

key_numbers.metric: False positive rate among industrial alerts

structure_gain: LLM4PFA (path-constraint hybrid) vs Basic Prompt, same GPT-4o backbone: accuracy 0.50 -> 0.93 (+0.43), FPR_Recall 0.45 -> 0.98 (+0.53) (Table 2).
stop_detail: Ground truth established via two-round manual review by developers/code reviewers plus majority voting over 3 LLM runs; no automated or formal verification oracle.

title: Vulnerability Detection with Interprocedural Context in Multiple Languages: Assessing Effectiveness and Cost of Modern LLMs
structure_gain: Adding interprocedural context (callee/caller code) DEGRADED performance for most models -- e.g. GPT-4.1 Mini F1 dropped 0.8608 -> 0.6753 (Code-Only vs Code+Callees, C, same model/prompt/temperature=0); only Claude Haiku 4.5 was robust. Token usage nearly doubled (+102%) without proportional gains.
stop_detail: No grounding/verification mechanism; this is a pure prompting study -- LLM outputs are parsed via regex and compared to ReposVul ground-truth CVE labels.

title: Root-Cause-Driven Automated Vulnerability Repair

key_numbers.value: Kumushi preferred 47% vs Codex 27% (26% tied), sign test p=0.0065

structure_gain: Evidence-weighted ranked Functions-of-Interest context (call-graph traversal + dynamic traces + static dataflow) yields comparable oracle-based plausibility to Codex (85.4% vs 86.0%) but a higher root-cause-fix rate (84.9% vs 77.8%) and higher human preference (47% vs 27%) versus a frontier commercial coding agent lacking this pre-computed localization context (Section 4, Table 4).
stop_detail: Context is grounded via bounded bidirectional call-graph BFS (callers/callees) from crash-stack anchors, combined with AFL++ dynamic execution traces and static dataflow queries, consolidated into an evidence-weighted score ranking the top-20 Functions of Interest fed to the LLM alongside the sanitizer report (Section 3.1/3.3); patches are iteratively verified via ASan compilation, PoC replay, and test-suite execution, with failure output looped back to the agent (Section 3.3).

title: Antaeus: Hunting Repository-Level Logic Vulnerabilities via Context-Grounded LLM Reasoning

key_numbers.value: Claude: 15 vs 9 vs 9; GPT: 12 vs 8 vs 7

structure_gain: Removing either context source (local callee augmentation or repository-context bundle) roughly halves true-positive detections (Claude: 15->9/9; GPT: 12->8/7) at fixed LLM backbone (Table IV), directly isolating representation contribution.
stop_detail: Context-grounding is static and non-agentic: Tree-sitter extracts depth-one callee signatures/bodies and referenced macro/constant definitions (local augmentation), plus a once-per-repository five-section context bundle (system purpose, principal model, protected objects, information outputs, trust topology) serialized into a single structured LLM call per function (Section III-B, Fig. 1).
